title: Gold ETF Pricing: How SEBI is Ensuring Fairer Value for Investors
description: Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) sometimes traded at prices different from their actual gold value due to outdated reference pricing and fixed trading limits.

faq.a: A Gold ETF (Exchange Traded Fund) is an investment fund that tracks the price of physical gold. Its units are traded on stock exchanges like shares, offering a convenient way to invest in gold without holding the physical metal.

faq.q: Why did Gold ETF prices sometimes differ from actual gold value?
faq.a: The discrepancy arose because exchanges used outdated (T-2) Net Asset Value (NAV) to set daily price bands, and these bands were fixed. This prevented the ETF's market price from quickly adjusting to real-time changes in global gold prices.

faq.q: How has SEBI addressed this pricing issue?
faq.a: SEBI has mandated using the previous day's closing price (VWAP of last 30 minutes) as the base for price bands, introduced dynamic price bands that can expand, and implemented a pre-open call auction for Gold and Silver ETFs to improve opening price discovery.

faq.q: When do these new rules come into effect?
faq.a: The changes to ETF trading mechanisms (base price, dynamic bands, pre-open auction) are effective from September 1, 2026. Separately, the valuation of physical gold and silver by mutual funds using domestic spot prices became effective from April 1, 2026.

faq.q: Will this change my existing Gold ETF investments?
faq.a: For existing investors, these changes primarily mean improved price discovery and fairer transaction prices when buying or selling. It does not alter your existing units, their taxation, or the fundamental nature of your investment.

faq.q: Where can I find the official SEBI circulars on these changes?
faq.a: You can find official circulars and notifications on the SEBI website (https://sebi.gov.in) under the "Legal" or "Circulars" sections.

based_on.title: Why Your Gold ETF Sometimes Trades at a Price That Doesn't Match Its Actual Value: And How SEBI Just Fixed It
